In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of the polyols to the XI active-site is strongly pH dependent.

the polyol inhibitors of XI bind in a similar manner to the linear substrates, but with the added benefit that the polyols can form additional water-mediated contacts that improve their affinity for XI.
sorbitol binds in an orientation in which its O5 atom is protonated and its O1 hydroxy group is hydrogen-bonded to Asp257 at acidic pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polyols are not competitive inhibitors, but rather that they bind in a similar manner as the substrate and the products, with the exception that they have a different protonation state at the C5 position of the inhibitor.
the binding mode of sorbitol to XI at pH 7.7 is very similar to that of the substrate glucose, whereas the binding mode at acidic pH is different.
the polyols are not competitive inhibitors of XI but rather they act as non-competitive inhibitors, which is consistent with the observed binding of Mg(2+) to the enzyme.
